reading.body:
Elicit operates a research assistant for scientific literature that claims to cover over 125 million papers and serve more than 2 million researchers, positioning itself as distinct from general-purpose AI tools through customizable report generation and domain specificity.

The company's two MCP server offerings reveal a shift toward embedding human judgment into AI agent workflows. Both products center on human-in-the-loop approval mechanisms, one adding confirmation dialogs and capability diagnostics, the other adding formal audit trails and hosted review pages. This architecture suggests a bet that AI agents require persistent human oversight before taking actions in research contexts, where decisions about which papers to include or which data to extract carry consequences for the integrity of scientific work.

Elicit's focus on research rather than compute infrastructure or power systems means this data does not directly illuminate constraints on AI scaling. The MCP servers do not appear to be infrastructure offerings; they are thin clients for verification. The data covers neither Elicit's computational requirements, its hosting arrangements, nor its power consumption.

profile_text.body:
Elicit is an AI tool built for scientific research, offering capabilities to search, summarize, extract data from, and chat with a corpus the company describes as covering over 125 million papers. The company states the platform is used by over 2 million researchers across academia and industry. Elicit describes its reports as deeply customizable, allowing users to control which papers are included and what information those reports cover, positioning the product as distinct from more general AI tools. The held facts record Elicit as a research assistant product with noted applications in paper analysis, systematic review, and academic integrity.

The site's held facts also show two MCP server entries associated with Elicit, both focused on human-in-the-loop functionality for AI agents. The first, ai.elicitly/elicitly, provides confirmation and form dialogs alongside a capability doctor, while the second, ai.elicitly/pro, adds durable approvals backed by a hosted review page and audit trail. No litigation or SEC filings are recorded for the company.
